claims.claim: instantaneous daily mortality Z of 0.15–0.52 for 5–24-day larvae (cited as 'abstract')
claims.source_value: Z 0.15 (2007) to 0.52 (2006) per day, one catch curve per year for larvae pooled across ages 8–21 d (not 5–24 d); 2005 omitted (too few larvae)
claims.location: p. 12 (PDF p. 13), Results 'Mortality Rate'; methods p. 7 (PDF p. 8); Fig. 4, p. 13 (PDF p. 14)
claims.quote: Mortality ranged from 0.15 (2007) to 0.52 (2006) across all years except 2005
claims.conditions: Pelican Lake, Nebraska (332 ha, mean depth 1.3 m, Sandhills); larval (< 13 mm TL) perch caught by surface trawl (1-mm mesh) in daylight every 10 d, April–June 2004–2012; 'young and old larvae (across ages 8–21 d) were pooled to estimate mortality'; the descending limb of ln(abundance) on 1-d age classes, from a single sampling date near peak hatch each year, so losses include any gear avoidance or move to the littoral; Z fell with total zooplankton biomass and water temperature
claims.note: the values are not in the abstract — the '(abstract)' tag should go now that the full text is read; change the stage to 'larvae 8–21 d old (pooled)'

claims.conditions: 'young larvae' 5–14 d old; mean daily growth per 10-d hatching cohort, computed as (TL − 4.7 mm at hatch)/age from otolith daily ages (methods p. 6, PDF p. 7); 2004–2012
'old larvae' 15–24 d old (still < 13 mm TL): 0.09 (cohort 1 of 2008) to 0.39 mm/d (cohort 3 of 2012); no old larvae caught in 2005; same method as above

notes: Table 3.6-4's text (§3.6.5) puts Pelican Lake among 'crowded or food-short larvae' (0.14–0.5/d): consistent — the authors found mortality inversely related to total available zooplankton biomass (and temperature). The study also proposes two recruitment bottlenecks: just after hatch (hatch date and temperature) and in older larvae (temperature and zooplankton). Lake vegetation in July 2009: emergents 31 % (reeds 8.5, bulrushes 15.5, cattails 7.0 %), submersed 9.9 %, open water 59.1 %.
